output:
  html_document:
    self_contained: true

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
  fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.5, fig.path = "results/process_expansion/figures/"
)
attempts <- readRDS("results/process_expansion/recovery.rds")
```

## What was tested

F can follow a random walk whose annual changes are correlated across ages.
Ordinary age-based formulas can share or vary process SDs for F, N and M.
Spawning-time SSB accounts for mortality before spawning and supplies the same
parent biomass to stock–recruit models.

The study includes 100 isolated Gaussian replicates for each common/grouped
SD design for F, N and M, and 30 full assessments for each grouped design.
Full assessments use 30 years, eight ages, two surveys and known observation
log-SDs of 0.08. These informative synthetic data do not validate every stock.
All attempts and warnings are retained; no failed fit is rescued.

## Numerical success and recovery

```{r}
groups <- sub("_[0-9]+$", "", names(attempts))
summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(unique(groups), function(group) {
  a <- attempts[groups == group]
  data.frame(
    Design = group, Attempts = length(a),
    Passed = sum(vapply(a, function(x) isTRUE(x$numerical), logical(1))),
    Errors = sum(vapply(a, function(x) !is.null(x$error), logical(1))),
    `Hessian passed` = sum(vapply(a, function(x) isTRUE(x$pdHess), logical(1))), check.names = FALSE
  )
}))
knitr::kable(summary)
recovery <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(attempts), function(name) {
  d <- attempts[[name]]$recovery
  if (is.null(d)) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  d$design <- sub("_[0-9]+$", "", name)
  d
}))
coverage <- aggregate(covered ~ design + parameter, recovery, function(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE))
knitr::kable(coverage, digits = 2, col.names = c("Design", "Parameter", "95% interval coverage"))
```

Coverage uses attempts with available intervals, including numerically failed
fits if intervals were returned. Errors remain in the numerical-success
denominator. SD coefficients are on the log-SD scale. Correlation intervals
use its unconstrained transformation; they are not truncated Normal intervals.

```{r}
full <- recovery[startsWith(recovery$design, "full"), ]
par(mar = c(5, 11, 4, 2) + .1)
for (component in c("F", "N", "M")) {
  d <- full[full$design == paste0("full_", component, "_grouped"), ]
  d$error <- d$estimate - d$truth
  d$parameter <- factor(d$parameter,
    levels = c("(Intercept)", "age_groupyoung", "rho_f"),
    labels = c("Older log SD", "Young/older log SD", "Age correlation")
  )
  boxplot(error ~ parameter, d,
    horizontal = TRUE, las = 1,
    main = paste(component, "process: parameter recovery"),
    xlab = "Estimate minus generating value", ylab = ""
  )
  abline(v = 0, col = "grey50", lty = 2)
}
```

All 690 fits passed numerical checks. Full-assessment median older/young SDs
were 0.199/0.101 for F, 0.203/0.097 for N and 0.199/0.085 for M, compared with
generating values of 0.20/0.10. Some young-age M SDs approached zero. Wide
intervals and convergence should not be mistaken for precise M recovery.
F age-correlation interval coverage was 26/30 in full assessments; these
small experiments do not establish generally calibrated uncertainty.

## Interpretation

These informative Gaussian and full-assessment experiments establish useful
recovery examples, not general identifiability or calibrated uncertainty for
sparse assessments. Inspect correlation and SD intervals separately from
numerical convergence. Historical stock-specific application trials remain in
Git history; maintained stock recipes and source notes describe current models.
